In `Q4VoltaDp4aSchedule` (defined in `src/ops/linear/q4/q4_volta_dp4a_gemm.cuh`):

- **`kTileN = 64`** — output rows per CTA (the lane axis, stride 32)
- **`kTileT = 128`** — tokens per CTA (the warp axis, stride `kNWarps` = 8)

`kStrideW` is **17** (i.e. `kWordsK + 1` = 16 + 1).

It is odd so that the 32 lanes, each reading a *different* weight row at the same column offset, land in 32 distinct shared-memory banks — an even stride of 16 words (64 bytes) would wrap every row back to bank 0 and produce a 32-way conflict on every int32 weight read.

The constant is **`kQ4Dp4aMinT`**, defined in `q4_launch.h` with the value **128**.

It is the minimum token width at which the graph-shard prefill GEMMs switch from the fp16 mma route to the int8/dp4a route, because the dp4a kernel's 128-token CTA tile only amortises its quantisation pass and shared-memory staging at that width and above.

The **int8 dp4a kernel** (`launch_q4_volta_dp4a`).

The dispatch in `q4_linear_swiglu_graph_shard_launch` checks the branches in order, and the dp4a branch is guarded by `t >= kQ4Dp4aMinT`. Since `kQ4Dp4aMinT = 128` and the chunk width is 2048, the condition `2048 >= 128` is true, so execution enters the dp4a branch and returns before the `t >= 16` mma branch is ever evaluated.

Per 64-element group, `Q5RowSplitStorage` defines:

- **`kCodeBytesPerGroup = 32`** — the low-nibble plane (4 bits per weight × 64 weights / 2 per byte)
- **`kHighBytesPerGroup = 8`** — the high-bit plane (1 bit per weight × 64 weights / 8 per byte)

`(high[K/8] >> (K%8)) & 1`

Each of the 8 high-plane bytes holds one bit per weight for 8 consecutive K values, so byte `K/8` is the byte covering weight K, and shifting right by `K%8` brings that weight's bit to position 0, where the `& 1` isolates it.

The Q5 5-bit decode (low nibble **plus** the high-plane bit) needs more live registers than the Q4 sibling's simpler 4-bit decode. Without the hint, the compiler allocates enough registers per thread that only **one** 256-thread block fits in a V100 SM's 65 536-register file, giving 8 warps / 64 max = **12.5 % occupancy**.

`__launch_bounds__(256, 2)` tells the compiler it must fit **two** such blocks per SM, capping the allocation at 65 536 / (256 × 2) = **128 registers per thread**. That forces the compiler to keep the decode register-frugal (the code comment notes it deliberately builds the packed int32 in a single accumulator rather than a `q[4]` array for exactly this reason), and the result is 16 warps / SM = **25 % occupancy** — matching what the Q4 sibling achieves naturally with its lighter decode.

```cpp
attn_q4_dp4a_prefill_enabled() && t >= kQ4Dp4aMinT &&
                   q4_volta_dp4a_supported(qk_out.ne[0], k, t)
```

This is the `else if` condition in the first scoped block (the query_key / Q4 projection). It requires three things simultaneously:

1. The `NINFER_NO_DP4A` environment-variable override is not set (`attn_q4_dp4a_prefill_enabled()` returns true).
2. The token width meets the dp4a minimum (`t >= kQ4Dp4aMinT`, i.e. `t >= 128`).
3. The shape is structurally valid for the dp4a kernel (`q4_volta_dp4a_supported` checks `n > 0`, `t > 0`, `k > 0`, and `k % 64 == 0`).

It passes **`false`**.

The MLP down shard produces a plain (non-residual) partial `W@x`; the two cards' partials are later summed together with the residual by a separate `residual_add_two` step, so the GEMM itself must not read-and-add the pre-existing value in `out`.

At a prefill chunk of T = 2048 (well above `kQ4Dp4aMinT = 128`), **every** quantized GEMM in the dual-device prefill forward takes the int8 dp4a route. None fall back to the fp16 mma kernel.

| Projection | Weight format | GEMM | Route at T = 2048 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **MLP gate/up** | Q4 `[gate_up_rows, 5120]` | `launch_q4_volta_dp4a` | **dp4a** |
| **MLP down** | Q5 `[5120, shard_intermediate]` | `launch_q5_volta_dp4a` (add_residual = false) | **dp4a** |
| **Attn query_key** | Q4 `[qk_rows, 5120]` | `launch_q4_volta_dp4a` | **dp4a** |
| **Attn gate_value** | Q5 `[gv_rows, 5120]` | `launch_q5_volta_dp4a` (add_residual = false) | **dp4a** |
| **GDN qk** | Q4 `[4096, 5120]` | `launch_q4_volta_dp4a` | **dp4a** |
| **GDN value** | Q5 `[6144, 5120]` (rows 0–6143) | `launch_q5_volta_dp4a` (offset 0) | **dp4a** |
| **GDN z** | Q5 `[6144, 5120]` (rows 6144–12287) | `launch_q5_volta_dp4a` (offset 6144) | **dp4a** |

The fp16 mma route (`launch_q4_volta_mma` / `launch_q5_volta_mma`) is the **fallback** for the intermediate band roughly T ∈ [16, 127], where the dp4a kernel's 128-token CTA tile would be mostly empty and its one-time int8 quantisation pass would not amortise. At T = 2048 every dispatch's `t >= kQ4Dp4aMinT` guard is satisfied, so the dp4a branch is taken before the mma branch is ever evaluated.
